{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the JDBC source as a configurable Spring XD module using standard JDBC drivers, connection properties, polling, parameterized queries, and a configurable output format.",
    "Implement Redis and Kafka as Spring XD sink modules using the existing Spring XD module and message-channel abstractions rather than introducing a separate ingestion API.",
    "Use ZooKeeper ACL-based authorization with configurable authentication credentials, preserving compatibility with the existing ZooKeeper client and node-management code.",
    "Expose the Trigger abstraction as a stable extension point using a documented public interface or abstract base class, with validation and lifecycle behavior defined by the existing trigger execution model.",
    "Deliver the custom-module requirement as a working example module accompanied by developer-oriented documentation and build/configuration guidance.",
    "Enable HTTPS for the Admin server through the supported Spring Boot 1.1.x configuration and dependency update, including configurable keystore, password, protocol, and port settings.",
    "Diagnose the end-to-end test failure by reproducing the combined Grunt server and Protractor execution, then fix process, socket, shutdown, or readiness handling without weakening test assertions.",
    "Follow the existing project conventions for configuration, logging, error handling, serialization, dependency management, unit tests, integration tests, and documentation."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment targets the historical Spring XD codebase and its existing build, module, server, Admin UI, and test conventions rather than a modern Spring Boot or Spring Integration rewrite.",
    "Requirements do not specify exact payload schemas, delivery guarantees, transaction semantics, or performance targets; reasonable configurable defaults will be implemented and documented.",
    "The JDBC source supports common relational databases through externally supplied JDBC drivers; database-specific optimization and vendor-specific features are out of scope.",
    "Redis sink support covers the principal write operation and configurable key/value or serialized-message behavior, but not a complete Redis data-model abstraction.",
    "Kafka sink support covers publishing messages to configurable brokers and topics, with standard producer options and normal error propagation; advanced transactions and schema-registry integration are out of scope.",
    "ZooKeeper security is limited to securing zNode access through supported authentication and ACL mechanisms; a full ZooKeeper cluster hardening program, network encryption, and credential rotation service are out of scope.",
    "The trigger extension must remain backward compatible with existing built-in triggers and does not require a new trigger scheduling engine.",
    "The custom-module example will demonstrate the recommended structure, configuration, testing, packaging, and registration process; it is not intended to be production-grade business functionality.",
    "HTTPS testing will use a local self-signed certificate or test keystore and will verify representative Admin endpoints; certificate procurement and production PKI integration are out of scope.",
    "The existing CI environment and supported JavaScript, Node.js, Grunt, ZooKeeper, Redis, Kafka, and database test dependencies are available or can be run locally.",
    "Effort includes implementation, developer-authored tests, documentation, code review preparation, and local verification, but excludes project management, production deployment, and long-term maintenance.",
    "Activities are estimated as total person-hours performed by one developer; estimates are summed as labor effort and do not imply parallel execution."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing Spring XD architecture, module conventions, build files, security model, Admin server, trigger APIs, and test infrastructure; define interfaces, configuration properties, compatibility constraints, and implementation plans for all user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "JDBC source module",
      "activity_description": "Implement the native JDBC source, including connection and driver configuration, query and polling behavior, parameter handling, result mapping or serialization, lifecycle and error handling, unit tests, database-backed integration tests, and user documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 96
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Redis sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable Redis message writing, serialization and key/value handling, connection and pool configuration, error behavior, lifecycle management, unit tests, integration verification against Redis, and usage documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "ZooKeeper node security",
      "activity_description": "Add configurable ZooKeeper authentication and ACL application for relevant nodes, integrate security settings into startup and node-management flows, preserve compatibility for unsecured configurations where appropriate, and add unit and integration security tests plus operational documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Extensible Trigger abstraction",
      "activity_description": "Refactor or extend the Trigger abstraction into a supported custom implementation point, define lifecycle and invocation contracts, provide registration and configuration behavior, retain existing trigger compatibility, and add API, unit, and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Custom module example and guidance",
      "activity_description": "Create a representative custom module using the recommended project structure and conventions, verify that it builds and runs, and document creation, configuration, testing, packaging, and deployment steps for developers.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Kafka sink module",
      "activity_description": "Implement configurable Kafka publishing, producer properties, topic and partition-related options supported by the existing platform, serialization, error handling, lifecycle management, unit tests, broker-backed integration tests, and operational documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Combined Grunt server and end-to-end test fix",
      "activity_description": "Reproduce the socket hang-up failure when the server and Protractor tests run in one Grunt process, identify readiness or process/socket cleanup issues, implement the fix, and verify both combined and separated test execution paths.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Admin server HTTPS support",
      "activity_description": "Update the Spring Boot dependency and build configuration as required, add HTTPS and keystore properties, wire the Admin server configuration, preserve HTTP behavior where supported, and add configuration, endpoint, startup, and negative/positive verification tests with documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the full relevant unit, integration, module, security, Admin, and end-to-end test suites; diagnose and correct integration regressions; verify clean and configured builds across supported execution modes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Final code quality, packaging, and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Perform final code cleanup, API and configuration review, dependency/license checks, documentation review, packaging verification, release notes, and preparation of the completed increment for handoff.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 576
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the JDBC source as a configurable Spring XD module using standard JDBC drivers, connection properties, polling, parameterized queries, and a configurable output format.
Implement Redis and Kafka as Spring XD sink modules using the existing Spring XD module and message-channel abstractions rather than introducing a separate ingestion API.
Use ZooKeeper ACL-based authorization with configurable authentication credentials, preserving compatibility with the existing ZooKeeper client and node-management code.

Expose the Trigger abstraction as a stable extension point using a documented public interface or abstract base class, with validation and lifecycle behavior defined by the existing trigger execution model.
Deliver the custom-module requirement as a working example module accompanied by developer-oriented documentation and build/configuration guidance.
Enable HTTPS for the Admin server through the supported Spring Boot 1.1.x configuration and dependency update, including configurable keystore, password, protocol, and port settings.
Diagnose the end-to-end test failure by reproducing the combined Grunt server and Protractor execution, then fix process, socket, shutdown, or readiness handling without weakening test assertions.
Follow the existing project conventions for configuration, logging, error handling, serialization, dependency management, unit tests, integration tests, and documentation.
assumptions: The increment targets the historical Spring XD codebase and its existing build, module, server, Admin UI, and test conventions rather than a modern Spring Boot or Spring Integration rewrite.
Requirements do not specify exact payload schemas, delivery guarantees, transaction semantics, or performance targets; reasonable configurable defaults will be implemented and documented.
The JDBC source supports common relational databases through externally supplied JDBC drivers; database-specific optimization and vendor-specific features are out of scope.
Redis sink support covers the principal write operation and configurable key/value or serialized-message behavior, but not a complete Redis data-model abstraction.

Kafka sink support covers publishing messages to configurable brokers and topics, with standard producer options and normal error propagation; advanced transactions and schema-registry integration are out of scope.

ZooKeeper security is limited to securing zNode access through supported authentication and ACL mechanisms; a full ZooKeeper cluster hardening program, network encryption, and credential rotation service are out of scope.
The trigger extension must remain backward compatible with existing built-in triggers and does not require a new trigger scheduling engine.
The custom-module example will demonstrate the recommended structure, configuration, testing, packaging, and registration process; it is not intended to be production-grade business functionality.
HTTPS testing will use a local self-signed certificate or test keystore and will verify representative Admin endpoints; certificate procurement and production PKI integration are out of scope.
The existing CI environment and supported JavaScript, Node.js, Grunt, ZooKeeper, Redis, Kafka, and database test dependencies are available or can be run locally.

Effort includes implementation, developer-authored tests, documentation, code review preparation, and local verification, but excludes project management, production deployment, and long-term maintenance.
Activities are estimated as total person-hours performed by one developer; estimates are summed as labor effort and do not imply parallel execution.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD architecture, module conventions, build files, security model, Admin server, trigger APIs, and test infrastructure; define interfaces, configuration properties, compatibility constraints, and implementation plans for all user stories.

Implement the native JDBC source, including connection and driver configuration, query and polling behavior, parameter handling, result mapping or serialization, lifecycle and error handling, unit tests, database-backed integration tests, and user documentation.

Implement configurable Redis message writing, serialization and key/value handling, connection and pool configuration, error behavior, lifecycle management, unit tests, integration verification against Redis, and usage documentation.

Add configurable ZooKeeper authentication and ACL application for relevant nodes, integrate security settings into startup and node-management flows, preserve compatibility for unsecured configurations where appropriate, and add unit and integration security tests plus operational documentation.

Refactor or extend the Trigger abstraction into a supported custom implementation point, define lifecycle and invocation contracts, provide registration and configuration behavior, retain existing trigger compatibility, and add API, unit, and integration tests.

Create a representative custom module using the recommended project structure and conventions, verify that it builds and runs, and document creation, configuration, testing, packaging, and deployment steps for developers.

Implement configurable Kafka publishing, producer properties, topic and partition-related options supported by the existing platform, serialization, error handling, lifecycle management, unit tests, broker-backed integration tests, and operational documentation.
